For each user, retain paired hit indicators and compute d = hit_A − hit_B. The macro improvement is Δ = ¼ Σ_category mean(d). Recommended application: bootstrap 200 users with replacement within each category, keeping both models’ outcomes paired; recompute Δ and report a 95% percentile interval alongside category differences and win/loss counts. This preserves category weights and pairing ([paired-bootstrap reference](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/)). Exact McNemar tests on discordant hits provide a complementary prespecified comparison. One changed hit moves a category by 0.5 percentage points and the macro by 0.125 points. With fixed candidates and training seed, bootstrap intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on those choices; the observed benchmark score itself is deterministic.

Repeated checkpoint and architecture selection introduces winner’s optimism: the best validation score exploits validation noise. Ordinary bootstrap intervals around the selected winner do not correct this ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Cheap exploratory diagnostics can reselect checkpoints inside bootstrap samples and assess them on out-of-bag users using cached predictions; these remain conditional on the searched candidate set and cannot undo adaptive architecture search. Log all trials, checkpoint evaluations, failures and GPU seconds; prespecify selection and stopping rules. Independent confirmation requires freezing the complete procedure before the host’s untouched final evaluation. More training seeds on the same validation users assess training variability, not independent confirmation.

Retain the pinned evaluator and describe results explicitly as HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives. Sampled rankings can disagree with full-catalog rankings, so neither bootstrap precision nor validation gains establish full-catalog superiority ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Cached-outcome resampling needs no retraining, conserving the shared GPU budget; report exploratory uncertainty separately from the final held-out result.
